summary: Nicholas Schlaepfer presents Hyperspace, a decentralized AI network that operates without GPUs by aggregating computational resources from community members' personal computers. Their existing product, aios, is downloadable for Windows and Mac and uses llama CPP for inference, enabling chat experiences powered by remote nodes. Hyperspace believes in diverse, open source models over a single large closed-source model, advocating a mixture-of-experts approach for optimal AI experiences. The flagship self-titled product, hyperspace, integrates prompt engineering, a visual react flow interface, Python execution, and RAG-style web browsing. A fine-tuned model converts user queries into directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) in JSON format representing methodical plans. The product includes in-house web scraping using Puppeteer and Beautiful Soup to convert HTML to markdown for LLM consumption. A terminal-based node editor gives power users control to edit titles, task descriptions, expected outputs, and add nodes. The demo showcases 'hyper engine V3' as the DAG orchestration model. It uses Qwen2 Instruct for reasoning and Llama 3 70B for summarization, providing diverse synthesized answers. Python nodes execute in an integrated terminal. A virtual file system supports directory management. The product aims to provide core primitives for agentic behavior: memory, Python execution, planning, and code generation. Availability was announced via waitlist on Twitter at hyperspace AI.

sections.title: Introduction to Hyperspace and Decentralized Network
sections.summary: Nicholas Schlaepfer introduces himself as an AI engineer and presents Hyperspace, a decentralized AI network with no GPUs that uses community-contributed personal computer resources. Their existing product aios runs on Windows and Mac using llama CPP for inference. He emphasizes the belief in diverse open source models over a single closed-source model.

sections.title: Hyperspace Product Features and Architecture
sections.summary: Describes the self-titled hyperspace product combining prompt engineering, visual react flow, Python execution, and RAG-like web browsing. Features a fine-tuned model outputting agentic planning DAGs in JSON, in-house web scraping with Puppeteer and Beautiful Soup converting HTML to markdown, and a terminal-based node editor for power users.

sections.title: Product Demo Walkthrough
sections.summary: Video demo shows query submission generating a node editor view with nodes streamed from the hyper engine V3 DAG orchestration model. Users can edit titles, task descriptions, and expected outputs. Uses Qwen2 Instruct for reasoning and Llama 3 70B for summarization. Demonstrates Python execution in terminal and a virtual file system for agent primitives including memory, planning, and code generation.

sections.title: Availability and Closing
sections.summary: Announces the product will be available later in the week via waitlist, directing viewers to follow Twitter at hyperspace AI for updates.
